summary: A card for a forearm bracer that lies flat and blooms open. You cut it from one A2 sheet of card or felt — no glue, no hardware. Tap the card, land on this page, ask for a change to it.
license_note: CC BY-NC 4.0 covers this card's design — the petal geometry, the A2 cutting sheet and both card faces — and it is what the page's #vc-card block declares, read out of the SERVED page and not only the source (curl of https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/bloom/ on 2026-08-17: "license": "CC-BY-NC-4.0", "replication": "noncommercial"). It is not the repository's grant: LICENSE at the repo root is MIT and covers the code. Unlike most of NOTICE, this artwork IS this project's to grant; NOTICE withholds it from the MIT grant because the project had already granted it on NonCommercial terms in public while an unscoped MIT said otherwise — the landing page carries the tag "Cards 1, 2, 4 CC BY-NC-4.0", measured live today, and this is card 4. NOTICE names seven paths for this card: src/site/bloom/card-front.png, src/site/bloom/card-back.png, src/web/cards/bloom-front.png, src/web/cards/bloom-back.png, examples/bloom-card/designs/*.png, examples/bloom-card/assets/front_editorial.png, examples/bloom-card/assets/back_blueprint.png. The generated qr_*.png in that same assets/ directory is deliberately NOT withheld. Nothing in this manifest enlarges what NOTICE withholds, and nothing here re-grants what it removed: the only terms offered over those files are CC BY-NC 4.0's. The full legal code ships beside the card at examples/bloom-card/LICENSE, 19,347 bytes, sha256 41003d4a74749c0220e33dd415042164b5a1093ed401f36277234f772d22d3d0 — fetched from creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/legalcode.txt on 2026-08-17 and compared with cmp: byte-identical, so the sha NOTICE cites is confirmed rather than repeated. That file is NOT on the website (/bloom/LICENSE and /examples/bloom-card/LICENSE both 404 today), while NOTICE is (/NOTICE and /NOTICE.txt return 200, 16,032 bytes, the same size as the tracked file, naming this card's paths). REPLICATION IS "noncommercial", the word the #vc-card block uses: print it, cut it, remix it, teach with it, credit it — do not sell it. The page hands the artwork over ready to print (../studio/?template=pair%3Acarpal-bloom-front; the live studio app.js is byte-identical to src/web/app.js and carries carpal-bloom-front and carpal-bloom-back), so the permission and the thing it permits sit one element apart on the same page, and since commit d26f023 the build fails if a page carries a print link its replication field does not allow.
origin: Not a fork and not a repository of its own: /bloom/ is a page-project inside mrdirno/vibe-cards, published on that repo's Pages surface (GitHub API read anonymously 2026-08-17, x-ratelimit-limit 60: fork=false, private=false, spdx_id MIT, created 2026-08-10T04:18:51Z). The page, the composition script examples/bloom-card/tools/build_card.py and this manifest are this project's work. THE DESIGN AND BOTH IMAGES ARE NOT — the package was generated somewhere else and taken in. tools/intake_card.py exists for exactly that and opens "Take a card package built somewhere else and wire it into this system." The originating system's own series log ships inside a sibling package, examples/aurelia-card/docs/AUTONOMOUS_HIERARCHY_LOG.md, and names this card "CARD 03 — CARPAL BLOOM BRACER 02 — PB-48-93-13" with its parameters (12-petal phyllotaxis on the 137.5° golden angle, Vogel r=c√(i+1), T-lock 12x9 into a 12.4x1.4 slot, Tyvek/rPET-felt material stack) and lists "image_gen editorial + blueprint" among the tools it mobilised. PB-48-93-13 is the join: it is RUN_ID at examples/bloom-card/tools/build_card.py:57 and "run_id" in the shipped package's #vc-card block. The same log records the address the card arrived carrying — https://kikko.craftworks/tool/CARPAL-BLOOM-002?tap=1#wish-it-better — and that host does not exist: dig returns no A, no NS and no SOA record, and `craftworks` has no NS either (measured 2026-08-17). The QR was regenerated for the real url with tools/make_qr.swift; ./tools/qrdecode returns https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/bloom/ from examples/bloom-card/designs/back_85.6x53.98mm_600dpi.png, src/site/bloom/card-back.png and examples/bloom-card/assets/qr_placeholder.png, run today. The package entered this tree 2026-08-15 (commit 8d56058, "Two more cards for the book, and the dropdown now has a folder for it instead of filing them next to strangers"). ITS NUMBER MOVED AND THE OLD ONE IS PRINTED: the generator's drop folder was CARPAL_BLOOM_BRACER_02 and the card was built for slot 003; MOKU-003 took that slot; the face printed 03 in display type over an ID line reading CARPAL-BLOOM-002, which is AUREA-LATTICE-002's number, and the page went live saying "CARD 003 OF COMPOUND CRAFT" in seven places (commit c037dcd, 2026-08-15). The owner's call on 2026-08-16 made it card 004 in every surface (commit 4a2f914). Cards printed before that day still read 03 over an ID ending 002, are not recallable, and the page says so out loud. The front image is a generated render and the project DECLARES it shows no face and no real or identifiable person, on the page ("Where the images come from") and in the #vc-card provenance field; that is the project's declaration and not something this file measured. The back is a reduced drawing of the A2 cutting sheet, drawing PHB-14P-FP-001 rev A, produced by the same generator. examples/bloom-card ships no README and no docs/ of its own — only LICENSE, designs/, assets/, package/index.html and tools/build_card.py — so the arrival record is git plus the sibling package's log, and this field is the only place it is stated plainly.
_note: A page-project's manifest, following the shape of src/site/gt/wish-it-better.json, the only prior one: it lives at the surface's own url because the network gate fetches <listed url>/wish-it-better.json, so one repo can publish several manifests at several urls with different levels. tools/build_site.py keeps an authored node manifest verbatim ("kept, not derived") and only DERIVES one for an entry already in listed[] — which is why this file is hand-authored and committed before any listing: a derived manifest would be produced by the act of listing, and criterion 4 would be evidence of itself. Measured 2026-08-17 before this file existed: https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/bloom/wish-it-better.json returns 404 while the page returns 200 and https://mrdirno.github.io/vibe-cards/bloom/control-404-for-the-wish-well-gate returns 404, so the host discriminates and the 404 is real. Its live 200 waits on the next deploy, as GT-001's did. || L0 ON ITS THREE CLAUSES, EACH MEASURED. (1) The file is present: WISH_IT_BETTER.md is served 200 at the site root, 15,345 bytes, `diff` byte-identical to the tracked copy, and this page is a surface of that same repo and host. (2) The wish channel works and needs no account: THIS page carries its own wishing well, not the landing page's — the served HTML contains the data-wish-well marker (grep -c → 1) and the fine print reads "No account, no email, nothing to sign up for." It posts card_id CARPAL-BLOOM-004 to the same Supabase host, table (vibe_card_wishes), anon key and column set as the landing-page well, which tools/wishing_well_actions.log shows accepted real wishes and closed them on 2026-08-15; that identity was established by comparing the two SERVED pages, not by sending a wish, which would have written a row into a live queue. (3) There is a LICENSE: the repo root's is canonical MIT (licence API, anonymous, spdx_id MIT) and this card's own terms ship as the full CC BY-NC 4.0 legal code, verified byte-identical to Creative Commons' published text today. || NOT L1, on both of its clauses, refused on evidence rather than on doubt. "Wishes reach a terminal state": the machinery exists — tools/wishing_well.py moves new → building → shipped or declined and appends every mutation to tools/wishing_well_actions.log — but nothing shows a wish for THIS card reaching one. The log's 20 lines key rows by wish UUID and name no card (grep -ci bloom → 0), and an anonymous select on the queue returns HTTP 200 with [] because row-level security filters it, which is filtered absence and not absence. The loop demonstrably exists; that it has ever turned for this card is unproven. "Every shipped change carries an eval meeting §2": docs/EVALS.md, the file the evals field above names, contains zero occurrences of "bloom" or "CARPAL". The commit messages for this card do carry measurements and some of them are evals, but "every" is a claim I did not verify — and this card's history contains changes that shipped and were corrected afterwards on evidence the shipping change did not have (c037dcd, 4a2f914, both in origin). The standard's §7 says start at L0, and its own v1.0.1 amendment "earns nobody L2"; the seed repo declares L1 at its root and this page does not inherit that, exactly as GT-001 declares L0 under the same L1 root. || WISH_CHANNEL IS DELIBERATELY BARE, with no #wish fragment. tools/build_site.py's derived manifests append "#wish" to a node page url, and no node page in this site has an element with that id — 0 in the served /bloom/ page and 0 across src/site/*/index.html — while both gate arms strip the fragment before fetching, so the dead anchor would never be caught by a check and a card holder's agent would land at the top of the page. The page IS the well; the url alone is the honest route. || TWO THINGS A READER OF THIS FILE NEEDS. First, publishing mechanics: build_site.py FAILS the build when this file's level disagrees with the level badged for this card's entry in src/site/network.json, so if the panel badges anything other than L0 one of the two is wrong and neither should be edited quietly to match the other; and this card's registry entry should carry host_repo rather than repo, for the reason GT-001's entry records — verify_pages_artifact.mjs joins listed entries to the ROOT manifest by repo url and fails on level drift, and this repo's root manifest declares L1. Second, a gap in the card itself, stated here because no field above can carry it: the page instructs "Print the full sheet and cut from that", and no such sheet is published. There is no .svg, .pdf or download link on the page (measured 0 of each) and none in examples/bloom-card/, while three sibling cards ship theirs (examples/aurelia-card/assets/aurelia_corona_1to1_A2.svg, examples/zaria-card/assets/CRAFT-006-ZARIA-cut-1to1.svg and .dxf, examples/kaze-card/assets/KAZE-KIRI-007_1to1.svg) and docs/GESICA_DECK.md §4 states Book One's entry fee as "every card leaves behind a reusable tool, and it carries a 1:1 cutting file". The card back is a reduced drawing, which the page says is not a template. So the object this card is a handle for cannot currently be cut from anything this manifest can point to. || ALSO UNVERIFIED, AND NOT TREATED AS FALSE: no wish was sent through the well from this page; the front render's "no real person" status is the project's declaration, not this file's measurement; and the physical card is recorded in src/site/network.json as a LEDGER-DERIVED chip row (a chip write to this url from tools/card_ledger.py), which was not read back off a tag for this file.
